topics.label: Concept and scope of contracts under Chinese law
topics.scope: Covers the Chinese definition of a contract under Article 2, contract-like acts (covenant, unilateral and multi-lateral acts), reward advertisements, and what relationships the 1999 Contract Law applies to (excluding marriage and personal-status relationships, state sovereign acts, and property-law transfers); excludes the general doctrines and interpretation of terms.
topics.source_sections: 1.3 Features of Chinese contract law; 1.3.1 The concept of a contract (including covenant, multi-lateral act, unilateral act); 1.3.2 Advertisements of rewards; 1.3.3 Approaches for defining contracts; 1.4 Application of contract law (including 1.4.1–1.4.4); Case Studies 1.1–1.3; Self-tests 1.1–1.2; Activity 1.3

topics.label: Doctrines of Chinese contract law
topics.scope: Covers the guiding doctrines of articles 3–7 of the PRC Contract Law: freedom of contract and its limits, pacta sunt servanda with force majeure and fundamental change of circumstances, good faith duties, and public policy; excludes contract formation and remedies for breach.
topics.source_sections: 1.6 Doctrines of contract law; 1.6.1 Freedom of contract; 1.6.2 Pacta sunt servanda; 1.6.3 Doctrine of good faith; 1.6.4 Public policy; Online discussion 1.2; Example 1.1; Case Studies 1.4–1.5; Self-test 1.4

topics.label: Historical development of Chinese contract law
topics.scope: Covers the evolution of contract law from Hammurabi, Roman law and common law through late Qing, Republican and post-1949 China to the 1999 unified PRC Contract Law; excludes substantive doctrines and current application.
topics.source_sections: Chapter 1 General principles of contract law › 1.1 Contract law: some background; 1.2 Historical development of Chinese contract law; 1.2.1 Historical developments in other jurisdictions; 1.2.2 Historical developments in China; Online discussion 1.1
